seat.BEST_WHY: The floor in 1 is the most convincingly cut stone of the deck. In the lit band around the figure (x 200–500, y 460–620) the stones vary in width, the joints vary in darkness and thickness along a single course, and individual blocks carry different amounts of chip and stain, so the run reads as laid masonry rather than a stamped tile. The wall cap at y 395–450 has a drawn beam-and-pin band with a darker underside, and the lighting falloff is held in check: the figure's halo is bright but the stones beside the brazier at (575–625, 525–565) keep their joints instead of blowing to white. The brazier itself is a tight sprite with a dark ring and red-black embers, scaled to the floor's pixel grid. It is also the frame with the fewest objects that ignore the light.
seat.WORST_WHY: 3 is a flat, stamped tileset with no lighting at all. The grey wall mass at top-right (x 256–384, y 0–110) is the same featureless grey plate repeated with 1px joints and no value variation between tiles; the same plate forms the bottom band (y 200–260). The dirt floor (x 50–250, y 0–200) is a red-brown noise texture with no drawn features, repeating visibly. The water (x 250–330, y 0–190) is one scale-pattern tile repeated with a hard straight edge against the dirt and no bank. The moss blobs at (330–384, 20–60) and (40–60, 100–120) are soft-edged, semi-transparent circles smoother than the pixel grid, i.e. a brush dabbed over the tiles. The chests at (65–95, 5–25) and (65–95, 50–70) are plain beige rectangles with a dark base. The figure at (215–235, 0–25) casts no light and nothing darkens with distance, so the "carried light" premise is simply absent. There is also no consistent wall convention: the north walls are bare grey tops with no face, while the south wall at y 260–288 shows a dark brick face.

panel.ruling: five seats; block only on strong-majority regression (>=4 of 5 rank below the reference); else install if exit met and plant caught. Rank-in-deck cannot resolve polish-sized deltas at a 40% flip rate. — Rafe, 2026-09-09
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.
